title: 6x 850ml Yabby Insulated Stainless Steel Tumblers with Handle $69.95 (Delivered) @SEC
body:
Deal: 6x 850ml Yabby Insulated Stainless Steel Tumblers with Handle $69.95 (Delivered) @SEC

[Daniel Plainview] Nothing to do with the vendor (who is excellent, having bought from them many times!) but very odd the makers of these claim to use copper lining in them. That would seem like the last thing you'd want in a thermos type vessel as copper is obviously an excellent thermal conveyor/transporter e.g moves heat or cold through it very well.
In a thermos you want the exact opposite e.g insultative qualities.
Doubling down on this the blurb on the makers website which details why they do this makes IMHO no sense whatsoever:
Our triple-layer insulation system uses two layers of 18/8 food-grade stainless steel with a copper layer in between to reduce heat transfer and maximise temperature control. This keeps drinks colder (or hotter) for longer, without condensation on the outside.
How they think Copper would reduce heat transfer - when thats exactly what it does best is beyond me. Either something major lost in comms or is a marketing wank - vacuum flasks were called that as to stop heat transfer they had a literal airless void in between their walls but these guys claim to have this filled with copper. Go figure.
[ratmanuwu] maybe it is really low quality copper and thus has worse heat transfer

[caprimulgus] I believe they are using copper as a lining due to low emissivity (lower than the stainless). The air/vacuum is the insulation - the copper is just minimising the heat transfer (radiated heat) on the air/vacuum side.
The copper will transfer heat quickly on the liquid side - but only until equilibrium. Once it hits the same temp as the liquid, it will stop, because there is no heat dissipation (like there would be fans/cooling on a heat sink). I think they are suggesting that the copper is acting as a thermal regulator by reaching equilibrium witb the liquid, and then helping to hold the liquid at a steady temperature. That seems to be what they are suggesting anyway.
So yes - copper conducts heat well, so doesnt intuitively make sense as an insulation material. But it's the air/vacuum that is the real insulator here, I believe.
(I believe the comms has just left out the air/vacuum in their description of the layers - but it does say "triple walled vacuum insulation" elsewhere.)
